problem: Existing audio-visual navigation methods fuse audio and vision by simple concatenation or late fusion, with no explicit representation of the target's relative position, and visual encoders receive no auditory guidance. This hurts learning efficiency and generalization to unheard sounds and unseen scenes.
motivation: Humans first estimate a sound's direction and distance and then use that intent to steer visual search. Regression of continuous coordinates is unstable under echoes and multimodal distributions, while attention-based fusion adds parameters and complicates RL optimization. A discrete spatial prior combined with lightweight channel-wise conditioning could address both issues.
key_idea: Predict discretized direction and distance distributions of the sound source as a compact spatial descriptor, then use audio embedding plus descriptor to generate FiLM-style channel scale and bias that modulate visual features before the recurrent policy.
insight: Both modules help on their own: in the Unheard ablation, Matterport3D SR rises from 33.5 (baseline) to 56.2 (w/o SDLD or w/o ACVF) and to 58.3 with both, so the two are complementary. The largest gains are on unheard sounds (Matterport3D unheard SR 33.5 to 58.3), which suggests a geometric spatial prior generalizes better than raw audio features. FiLM fusion costs 4.50M/4.49M params against 7.06M/7.67M for spatial attention.
method: SDLD: fuses visual and audio feature maps into F_av, predicts softmax distributions over K=20 bins for distance (0-30 m) and angle (-pi to pi), and takes expectations to get d_hat and theta_hat

Cartesian encoding: converts the angle to (cos, sin) to avoid periodicity instability; a Sound Event Detection score s_t is also computed, and the triplet (s_t, x_t, y_t) is fed to an LSTM that outputs the spatio-temporal descriptor g_t
ACVF: an MLP Psi takes c_t=[F_a; g_t] and outputs per-channel gamma and beta; visual features become (1+gamma)*F_v+beta, broadcast over spatial positions
Policy: the modulated visual features feed a GRU with an Actor-Critic head that outputs actions and values, trained with PPO from scratch

setting.backbone: SoundSpaces-style CNN visual/audio encoders + SDLD (LSTM) + FiLM MLP + GRU actor-critic (trained from scratch with PPO)
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces Replica (9/4/5 train/val/test scenes) and Matterport3D (73/11/18); RL from scratch, 5 parallel envs, 40,000 PPO updates, no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB or depth image + binaural audio spectrogram
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions (SoundSpaces: move forward, turn left, turn right, stop)
setting.privileged: none stated (GT source position is presumably used as a supervision signal for SDLD during training; not explicit)

numbers_note: The paper does not say which split (val or test) is evaluated; 'test' is assumed from the test scene group. Heard/Unheard and Replica/Matterport3D are separate settings, listed as separate entries.
results: With depth input, SACF beats SoundSpaces and AGSA on SPL/SR nearly everywhere. Replica Unheard SR is 79.1 vs 50.9 for SoundSpaces, and Matterport3D Unheard SPL/SR is 42.4/58.3 vs 26.2/36.5 for AGSA. SNA on Replica is slightly below AGSA (51.7 vs 52.0 Heard, 18.7 vs 22.4 Unheard). The RGB variant also beats the SoundSpaces RGB baseline.
limitations: Single fixed random seed, with no variance estimates; the baseline set is small (mainly SoundSpaces and AGSA)
Evaluation is simulation only, with no real-robot tests; SNA on Replica trails AGSA
The ablation reports only the Unheard setting, and the efficiency claims (FPS, RTF) come with limited hardware detail
